attempts.raw_response: If your arms start to ache, take a short break and shake out your hands before continuing. Many people find it easier to work on the back sections while sitting down, with a mirror positioned behind them. Another option is to ask a friend to help with the harder-to-reach areas. Once all your braids are finished and trimmed, you can style them as desired. Leave them loose, pull them back into a ponytail, or pin them up for a more formal look. With practice, the entire process becomes much faster and the results look more polished. Don't be discouraged if your first attempts seem uneven. Each time you complete this technique, your hands will grow more confident and the braids will come together more smoothly.

pair.human_continuation:
Remember to take breaks, especially if your arms start to feel sore. You can use the same color of extension for each cornrow, or you can add a few colored ones for a unique look. Use your fingers to apply some hydrating hair cream to the fine hairs at your hairline. Smooth them down and back with a soft bristle brush.
Take your first section and divide it into three smaller sections. Cross the left section over the middle one, then cross the right section over the middle one. Fold the thinnest kanekalon strand in half, and bring it around the back of your head. The looped part should be facing your hairline and the two tails should be hanging down the back of your head.
pair.prefix: Tuck the tail under the elastic, then wrap the elastic a few more times. This conceals the end without having to deal with heat-sealing. You may have noticed that there are some hairs sticking out of the folded end of your braid. This is perfectly normal. Use a small pair of scissors to trim away any stray strands. This can get tiring, especially if you are doing it by yourself.
